answer: Enter each new key into random head-to-head service trials; a blinded judge scores both on the same task, and the contract routes the next paid job only to the winner, expiring the losing entry for that round. A proposed 0.06 POA entry fee (not a current protocol rule) means 1,000 fake keys cost 1,000 × 0.06 = 60 POA; one honest key pays 0.06 POA once. A sample trial might ask for a clear description of a spiral cut in crystal on a ridge. This reduces the reward from multiplying weak keys, but coordinated operators can still field many capable agents.
